text: When a family cancels partway through the year, Scout compares what they've paid this membership year with the covered services they've used.
Remember: read the preview to the owner before you cancel. If they used more than they paid, the difference is charged to their card.
Only lead client liaisons, managers and admins can cancel a membership. If a family asks you, pass it on to them.
Maria is moving out of our area, and wants to cancel Maple's plan. Click Cancel.
First, the sentence the owner will see. Read it to her.

Maria has paid sixty-nine dollars this membership year, and Maple has already used four hundred thirty-two dollars in covered services: her wellness exam, trip fee, vaccine and heartworm test. Under the membership agreement, she owes the difference.
Below that, each payment and each covered service that went into the numbers.
If a family has used less than they paid, the unused part isn't refunded, unless the practice makes an exception.
Scout confirms what happens: the membership ends now, and the amount owed is charged to Maria's card.
Scout opens Maria's account on the settlement record, with the amount charged for the covered services. Stripe billing stops, and she gets an email with the breakdown.
Back on Maple's chart, the Membership section now says she isn't on a plan.

The most common mistakes: cancelling in the Stripe dashboard, which Scout never hears about, and using Cancel when a pet has died. That has its own steps. Remember: read the preview to the owner before you cancel.
